evidence: Receiving DO2: 9.55 mg/L at t=50.0 h vs 1.00 mg/L at 50.2 h, 0.89 mg/L at 52.0 h — below 2.0 mg/L minimum (receiving_observations)
P assay: 3.11 g/L at t=48 h, comparable to source batches (~3.0 g/L), indicating active production worth retaining
Forward model: strong_feed_reduction post-decision below_limit_h=9.4, deficit=7.95, min DO=0.87 — best of all actions; increase_air worst (13.2 h, deficit 12.3)
Forward model product mass ~194 kg under all non-stop actions; stop yields zero counted production
Model-estimated receiving transfer multiplier ≈0.40, explaining why air increase alone is ineffective
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed step-wise at t=50.2 h from ~9.5 to ~0.9 mg/L and remains far below the 2.0 mg/L operating minimum through the 52.0 h decision point, while product formation is on track (P=3.11 g/L at 48 h). This pattern indicates a loss of oxygen-transfer capacity in the receiving vessel, not a feed-driven demand spike. Among the bounded interventions, the source-calibrated forward model shows strong_feed_reduction (feed ×0.6, air ×1.15) is the best available response: it yields the fewest below-limit hours (9.4 vs 11.4–15.2), the smallest oxygen deficit (7.95 mg·h/L vs 8.40–13.24), and the highest minimum DO2 (0.87 mg/L vs 0.71–0.80), while retaining essentially the full ~194 kg product mass and the highest terminal concentration (2.50 g/L). No action restores DO2 to ≥2 mg/L per the model (the transfer loss dominates), so this is the least-infeasible option that keeps counted production nonzero; a stop would forfeit all counted product, and increase_air alone is the worst option since ×1.15 aeration cannot compensate for a ~60% transfer impairment.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal/source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; its sensitivity set shows minimum DO2 ranging 0.45–1.29 mg/L under strong_feed_reduction, so feasibility (DO2 ≥ 2.0) is not achieved in any modeled member. Actual receiving kinetics, the cause of the transfer loss, and whether DO2 recovers after feed reduction are unknown. The step-like DO2 drop could also partly reflect a sensor fault, but treating it as real is the safe interpretation. Product mass estimates carry ±~20 kg model spread.
